items.actClause:
AN ACT to create a veterans' mental health and suicide prevention task force;
and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1788

SPONSOR: SANDERS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to create a veterans' mental health and suicide prevention task
force; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration
thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To creates a veterans' mental health and suicide prevention task force.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 states legislative intent.

Section 2 provides for the creation of the task force, including how
members are appointed and what the task force's roles are (e.g., study
current practices, recommend mental health practices and suicide
prevention efforts).

Section 3 provides the act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after
it shall have become a law and expire May 1, 2023.

 
EXISTING LAW:

New Law

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legislature is concerned with the health, safety, and welfare of all
returning veterans of the United States armed forces to New York and the
high rate of mental health problems and suicides of members of the
United States armed forces.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2015 Referred to Senate Veterans,Homeland Security and Military Affairs

2016 Referred to Senate Veterans,Homeland Security and Military Affairs

2017 Referred to Senate Veterans,Homeland Security and Military Affairs

2018 Referred to Senate Veterans,Homeland Security and Military Affairs

2019 Passed Senate

2020 passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become a law and shall expire May 1, 2023 when upon such date the
provisions of this act shall be repealed.

AN ACT to create a veterans' suicide prevention temporary task force; and

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1788A

SPONSOR: SANDERS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to create a veterans' suicide prevention temporary task force;
and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To creates a veterans' suicide prevention temporary task force.   
SUMMA-
RY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 states legislative intent.

Section 2 provides for the creation of the temporary task force, includ-
ing how members are appointed and what the task force's roles are (e.g.,
study current practices of those who have served on active military
duty, recommend mental health practices and suicide prevention efforts
for those who have served on active military duty).

Section 3 provides the act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after
it shall have become a law and expire August 31, 2024.

 
EXISTING LAW:

New Law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legislature is concerned with the health, safety, and welfare of all
returning veterans of the United States armed forces to New York and the
high rate of mental health problems and suicides of members of the
United States armed forces.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017: referred to Veterans' Affairs
2018: amended and referred to Veterans' Affairs
2019: referred to Veterans' Affairs
2020: amended and referred to Veterans' Affair

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become a law and shall expire August 31, 2024 when upon such date the
provisions of this act shall be repealed.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 130 Chapter 770
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 1788-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  create  a  veterans' suicide prevention temporary task
        force; and providing for the  repeal  of  such  provisions  upon
        expiration thereof"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill creates a Veterans' Suicide Prevention Temporary Task Force
that would examine and study the current  mental  health  practices  and
suicide  prevention efforts for those who have served on active military
duty. The health, safety, and welfare of  all  veterans  of  the  United
States  Armed  Forces  is  of  paramount  concern  to my administration.
Therefore, I have reached an agreement with the  Legislature  to  ensure
that  the appointments to this task force are well suited to address the
high rate of mental health problems  and  suicides  of  members  of  the
United States Armed Forces.
 
  Based on this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
